# phase-110 — Let `this` be the operand of `at` and `of`, so a worded index works inside an object method

## You must change `src/ or bootstrap/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/ or bootstrap/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
src/parser.rs:1813 `fn kind_starts_operand` matches Number | Text | YesNo | Nothing | Identifier | LeftParen | LeftBracket | LeftBrace | Not | Minus | To, and does NOT match `TokenKind::This` - while src/parser.rs:2575 `parse_primary` has a `TokenKind::This =>` arm that reads `this` as an ordinary primary. The two disagree, so `this` is a primary everywhere except as the operand of a worded index or worded length. Verified against the built binary this audit (`target/debug/rb`, HEAD c8156ab): inside a method, `return length of this` raises `ParserError: Expected something to measure after \`length of\`` at the column of `this`, while `return length of nothing` in the identical position parses and runs, and `return this.xs at this` raises `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'at'; did you mean 'as'?` - the `at this` split into two statements, which is the same misparse phase-080 was created to end. `this.xs at 0` works (prints 10) because `at` is reached through the normal expression path; only the worded OPERAND is blind. Both engines fail identically (bootstrap/compiler.rb:1146 omits `this` from its operand table the same way, while bootstrap/compiler.rb:2177 parses it), so tests/differential_test.rs and the S3 fixed-point test compare two wrong answers and cannot see it. This is LIVE on main: logs/phase-080.review.3.log ends `REVIEW VERDICT: FINDINGS 1` naming this exact file:line, and phases/phase-080/.done was still written at 06:51 - see phase-111.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make `this` a legal operand of `at` and `of` in both engines, so `length of this` and `xs at this` are read as one expression instead of being refused or split into separate statements.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `return length of this` inside an object method is an index/length expression, not `ParserError: Expected something to measure` - it must reach the same runtime check `length of nothing` reaches
- [ ] `return this.xs at this` raises a clean positioned Runtime or Analyzer error naming the problem, and NEVER `Unknown variable 'at'` - the `at this` is no longer split into separate statements
- [ ] `rb run` and (`rb compile` then `rb vm`) agree on every case above, byte for byte in outcome
- [ ] `bootstrap/compiler.rb` operand table and src/parser.rs:1813 operand table list the same token kinds, and a test asserts the two tables agree rather than a human reading both
- [ ] the already-working `this.xs at 0`, `xs at 0` and `xs[0]` keep their behaviour, each pinned by a test
- [ ] edge_* tests cover: `length of this` with a zero-field object, one field, many fields; `this.xs at this`; `this` as operand of `at` inside a nested object; `this` inside a function literal nested in a method; and the same cases through the bytecode engine
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and the S3 fixed-point test still passes
